questions.questionText: If coagulant (Alum) dosage is fixed, then the best condition for coagulation process is:
questions.explanationHtml:
(d)
• High Turbidity and High Alkalinity water is easy to treat as alum will react properly due to
proper alkalinity and flocs will form steadily.
• pH will be affected temporarily but treatment will be effective.
• High turbidity and low alkalinity water may need lime to improve alkalinity and optimize coagulation.
• Low turbidity and low alkalinity water is difficult to treat, requiring alkalinity correction
with lime and high doses of high molecular weight polyelectrolyte.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: Which of the following is not a recognised limitation of the classical sag curve model used to predict dissolved oxygen levels in streams?
questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a recognised limitation of the classical sag curve model used to predict dissolved oxygen levels in streams?

options.html: It fails to consider the spatial variation in BOD decay due to algal respiration and nitrification.
options.text: It fails to consider the spatial variation in BOD decay due to algal respiration and nitrification.

options.html: It overlooks the contribution of microbial films attached to stream beds in oxygen consumption.
options.text: It overlooks the contribution of microbial films attached to stream beds in oxygen consumption.

options.html: It underestimates the initial oxygen demand by assuming instant establishment of anaerobic conditions.
options.text: It underestimates the initial oxygen demand by assuming instant establishment of anaerobic conditions.

options.html: It does not incorporate the varying deoxygenation rate constants across different stream reaches.
options.text: It does not incorporate the varying deoxygenation rate constants across different stream reaches.

questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
• It is based on the assumption that there is one source of BOD when there may actually be several different point or non-point sources of BOD.
• Algal respiration in the absence of sunlight, nitrification processes that increase the oxygen demand and the presence of sludge deposits in pool areas can all increase a stream's BOD. It doesn't account for them.
• In shallow streams, masses of microbial growth attached to the streambed may consume more dissolved oxygen.
• It assumes steady-state conditions all along a river channel and does not incorporate varying
deoxygenation rate constants because of channel formation, obstacles, pools, etc.

questions.questionMarkup: In the analysis of nitrogen content in sewage, which one of the following interpretations is most appropriate if only free ammonia and albuminoid nitrogen are detected in significant amounts, while nitrates are absent?
questions.questionText: In the analysis of nitrogen content in sewage, which one of the following interpretations is most appropriate if only free ammonia and albuminoid nitrogen are detected in significant amounts, while nitrates are absent?

options.html: The sewage is fully stabilised and has undergone complete treatment.
options.text: The sewage is fully stabilised and has undergone complete treatment.

options.html: The sewage is freshly discharged and has not undergone significant decomposition.
options.text: The sewage is freshly discharged and has not undergone significant decomposition.

options.html: The sewage is in the intermediate stage of stabilisation.
options.text: The sewage is in the intermediate stage of stabilisation.

options.html: The sewage has high nitrate-reducing bacteria activity.
options.text: The sewage has high nitrate-reducing bacteria activity.

questions.explanationHtml:
(b)
• The free ammonia indicates the very first stage of decomposition of organic matter (thus indicating recently staled sewage).
• Albuminoid nitrogen indicates quantity of nitrogen present in sewage before the decomposition of organic matter has started.
• Nitrates indicate the most stable form of nitrogenous matter contained in sewage, thus indicating the well-oxidized and treated sewage.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: Which of the following statements about oxidation/stabilization ponds is/are correct?
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about oxidation/stabilization ponds is/are correct?

options.html: Facultative ponds have both aerobic and anaerobic zones.
options.text: Facultative ponds have both aerobic and anaerobic zones.

options.html: Fully aerobic ponds are difficult to construct and operate.
options.text: Fully aerobic ponds are difficult to construct and operate.

options.html: Oxidation ponds lead to an increase in BOD due to algal production.
options.text: Oxidation ponds lead to an increase in BOD due to algal production.

options.html: Effluents from oxidation ponds are not suitable for land irrigation.
options.text: Effluents from oxidation ponds are not suitable for land irrigation.

questions.explanationHtml:
(a, b)
• In a facultative pond, the upper layers work under aerobic conditions, while the anaerobic
conditions prevail in the bottom layer.
• The totally aerobic ponds will have to be of very small depths and still then may require
occasional stirring, to prevent anaerobic conditions in the settled sludge.
• The production of algae and oxidation of organic matter result in a net reduction in BOD,
since algae are more stable than the original organic content.
• The Effluents from oxidation ponds can be easily used for land irrigation, especially in places
where direct discharge into rivers is not feasible.
